output.subject: A 40-foot containerised modular vertical farm growing year-round leafy greens (lettuce, herbs, brassicas) for the United Kingdom market. LED grow-lights with daily light integral control, climate and carbon-dioxide dosing, recirculating nutrient system, IoT sensor mesh feeding a remote farm-management dashboard. Designed to ship complete on a flatbed lorry, plug into a three-phase mains supply, and run unattended between weekly plantings.

A premium walking stick for the United Kingdom market — working name Sentinel — with invisible falls-detection and gait-analysis intelligence. Wood handle (ash or walnut, machined and finished), carbon-fibre shaft, rubber and tungsten ferrule, adjustable length, weight target 450 grams or under. The intelligence is invisible to the user: 9-axis inertial measurement unit and capacitive grip sensor in the handle, pressure sensors at handle and ferrule, cellular module and battery in a tubular cavity in the upper shaft, speaker / microphone / haptic on the underside of the handle. brief.whyNow: The UK ageing population is driving record NHS falls-related costs (£3,000–£10,000 per prevented fall); LTE-M/NB-IoT network coverage has matured to support always-on low-power cellular without smartphone dependency; UK MDR and UKCA post-Brexit regulatory frameworks create a defined Class I launch path with a clear upgrade route to Class IIa; and NHS direct-payments and integrated-care-system commissioning mechanisms now provide a scalable B2B channel alongside direct-to-consumer.
brief.mission: Sentinel is a premium walking stick that provides invisible falls detection and gait analysis for older adults in the United Kingdom, delivered through always-on cellular connectivity to a family-facing companion app and a 24/7 alarm receiving centre.
brief.useCase: An adult child buys Sentinel for their parent; the parent uses it as a conventional walking stick while the device silently monitors gait, detects falls, and sends location and weekly health summaries to the family via a companion app — with emergency escalation to a 24/7 alarm receiving centre requiring no action from the user.

A 40-foot containerised battery energy storage system delivering 3.5 MWh and 1.5 MW for behind-the-meter commercial and industrial sites in the United Kingdom. Lithium iron phosphate cells, integrated battery management, bi-directional power conversion with grid-forming capability, liquid-cooled thermal management, and certified fire detection and suppression. Target installed capital cost under 180,000 pounds. Must ship complete on a flatbed lorry, install on a prepared concrete pad, and commission inside two days. Compliant with United Kingdom G99 grid code and the latest National Fire Chiefs Council guidance for lithium battery storage.

brief.whyNow: UK grid code G99 now mandates grid-forming capability for new behind-the-meter storage connections; NFCC guidance on lithium battery storage has matured into a de-facto planning requirement; LFP cell costs have fallen sufficiently to make containerised C&I BESS commercially viable at scale; DNOs are actively incentivising demand-side flexibility.
brief.mission: Deliver a factory-integrated, containerised lithium iron phosphate battery energy storage system that enables UK commercial and industrial sites to optimise energy costs and support grid stability behind the meter, without specialist on-site build work.
brief.useCase: A prepared-pad, two-day-commission containerised BESS that ships complete on a flatbed lorry and connects behind the meter to reduce peak demand charges and provide grid services for UK C&I sites.

output.subject: A 40-foot containerised seawater reverse-osmosis desalination unit producing 500 cubic metres per day of potable water from seawater feed. Pre-treatment, two-pass reverse osmosis, post-treatment (remineralisation and chlorination), 50 per cent recovery rate, energy-recovery device on the brine stream. Target specific energy consumption under 3.5 kilowatt-hours per cubic metre. Designed for coastal disaster relief, remote-island municipal water, and construction-site freshwater supply. Target installed capital cost under 350,000 pounds. Must ship complete on a flatbed lorry, plug into a three-phase mains supply or local diesel genset, and start producing within four hours of arrival on site.

brief.whyNow: Increasing frequency of coastal humanitarian crises, island-community water insecurity, and remote-construction activity has created demand for rapidly deployable potable-water infrastructure that requires no civil works and can be mobilised within hours; advances in isobaric energy-recovery technology now make containerised SWRO viable at target energy and capital-cost thresholds.
brief.mission: To deliver containerised seawater desalination capability that can be transported on a standard flatbed lorry, connected to shore power or a diesel genset, and producing potable water within four hours of arrival on site — serving coastal disaster relief, remote-island municipalities, and construction operations.
brief.useCase: A self-contained 40-ft ISO container unit connects to seawater feed, three-phase power, and brine-discharge pipework on site and produces 500 cubic metres per day of chlorinated, remineralised potable water within four hours of lorry delivery.
